title: Counter Drone RF Analyzer / Drone DF Simulator
summary: A desktop application for uploading RF recordings, visualizing power spectra and spectrograms, and presenting AI-based drone-presence predictions with signal measurements.
problem: RF recordings need to be interpreted through spectrum views, signal measurements, and classification. This project brings those views together in a desktop analysis workflow.
intendedUsers: People exploring RF recordings, signal measurements, and drone-presence analysis.
approach: Upload an RF recording, inspect its power spectrum and spectrogram, then review the drone-presence prediction and confidence alongside RSSI, peak power, and noise-floor measurements.
contribution: Developed the desktop RF analysis project, bringing recording upload, signal visualization, AI-based drone-presence prediction, and signal readouts into one application.
challenges: Detailed development notes have not been added yet.
lessons: Detailed lessons learned have not been added yet.
status: Desktop project; the source repository is available on GitHub.
improvements: Proposed next steps: document the recording format and analysis workflow, add an example recording suitable for public sharing, and describe the model evaluation method.
imageAlt: Interface concept showing an RF spectrum, signal measurements, and a direction-finding radar.

title: LilNest — Maternal Care Platform
tagline: A little care. A big difference.
summary: A full-stack maternal-health web application built with React, Node.js, and MongoDB, with authentication, a responsive interface, and RESTful API integration.
problem: The project explores a maternal-care experience on the web, connecting a responsive frontend with authentication and a database-backed application.
intendedUsers: People seeking a maternal-care web experience.
approach: Connect a React interface to a Node.js backend and MongoDB database through RESTful APIs, with authentication and layouts that adapt to different screen sizes.
contribution: Built the full-stack application, including authentication, the responsive user interface, and RESTful API integration between the frontend and backend.
challenges: Detailed development notes have not been added yet.
lessons: Detailed lessons learned have not been added yet.
status: Web application with a live demo.
improvements: Proposed next steps: document the main user flows, review accessibility across screen sizes, and add a case study of the frontend and backend architecture.
imageAlt: Interface concept for a maternal-care platform using soft pink panels and a welcoming layout.

title: MotionBeatz — Gesture-Controlled Music Player
summary: A computer-vision-based music player that uses hand-gesture recognition to control playback, volume, and track navigation.
problem: Conventional music players use onscreen playback controls. MotionBeatz explores hand gestures as another way to control listening.
intendedUsers: Listeners interested in controlling music through hand gestures.
approach: Recognize hand gestures through computer vision and connect those gestures to playback, volume adjustment, and track navigation.
contribution: Developed the computer-vision-based music player and its gesture-driven playback, volume, and track-navigation controls.
challenges: Detailed development notes have not been added yet.
lessons: Detailed lessons learned have not been added yet.
improvements: Proposed next steps: add a short interaction demo, document the gesture vocabulary, and evaluate recognition across lighting conditions.
